get.summary:
`GET /tunnel` — read the current persisted settings + observed runtime as a
single wire snapshot. Gated by [`Scoped<LiveTunnelSettingsReader>`]: the
settings read lives behind the `wildflower/TunnelSettings.r` capability, so
this handler never touches the store directly (a `403` on an under-scoped
token). Collected into the `OpenAPI` doc via `routes!` in the parent module,
which reads this `#[utoipa::path]`.

put.summary:
`PUT /tunnel` — full-replace of the visible settings under the caller's
`revision` token. Gated by [`Scoped<LiveTunnelSettingsEditor>`]: the write
lives behind the `wildflower/TunnelSettings.u` capability, so this handler
never touches the store directly (a `403` on an under-scoped token).
put.description:
A stale revision returns 409 with the current snapshot so the client can
rebase; a winning write bumps the revision, reconciles the live supervisor,
then — like the launch seam — **awaits the liveness settling** (a `/health`
probe verifies, or the verify deadline elapses) before returning, so the
snapshot reflects *real* reachability rather than an optimistic `dialing`. A
no-op change (same dialable config on an already-up tunnel) returns
immediately `verified` — `reconcile` leaves the live tunnel untouched, so
there's nothing to wait for. A `publicHost` that isn't a bare `host[:port]`
is refused with a `400` before anything is written. Collected into the `OpenAPI` doc via `routes!`
in the parent module, which reads this `#[utoipa::path]`.

200.description: Write applied; the new snapshot after the daemon reconciled

400.description: `publicHost` isn't a bare `host[:port]` naming an `https://` origin; nothing was written

409.description: Stale revision; no write happened — the current snapshot is returned

get.summary:
`GET /tunnel/requests` — one page of the request log, newest first, with the
cursor for the next. Gated by [`Scoped<LiveRequestLogReader>`]
(`wildflower/TunnelSettings.r`).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The previous page's `nextCursor`: only requests older than it.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Only requests whose verified caller is this OAuth client.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Only requests from this client address.

parameters.name: refused
parameters.description:
`true` for only refused requests (a bearer gate's `401` or a scope
`403`), `false` for only the rest.

200.description: One page of the request log, newest first

get.summary:
`GET /tunnel/requests/callers` — who reached the server through the tunnel: one row
per (caller, client address), the group with the newest request first.
Gated by [`Scoped<LiveRequestLogReader>`] (`wildflower/TunnelSettings.r`).

200.description: The request log grouped by caller and client address, newest first

CallerSummaryBody.description:
What the request log holds for one (caller, client address) pair — a row of
`GET /tunnel/requests/callers`. The client's display name is not included; resolve
`clientId` through gatekeeper's client list.

clientId.description:
The verified caller's OAuth client, or `null` for the requests no
bearer gate verified.

address.description:
The visitor's address the trusted front recorded, or `null` when it
recorded none.

refusedCount.description: How many were refused: a bearer gate's `401` or a scope `403`.

oneOf.description: The newest request's refusal, or `null` when no bearer gate refused it.

InsufficientScopeBody.description:
Wire shape for a 403 — the caller authenticated, but their token doesn't cover
the scope(s) an operation requires. `missingScopes` names the scopes the
caller must additionally hold.

error.description: Always `"InsufficientScope"` — the discriminant a client switches on.

missingScopes.description: The rendered scopes the caller lacks.

InvalidPublicHostBody.description:
Wire shape for a 400 `InvalidPublicHost` — a `PUT /tunnel` whose
`publicHost` isn't a bare `host[:port]`. Matches the TS
`InvalidPublicHostSchema`.

LoggedRequestBody.description:
One request in the log — an element of `GET /tunnel/requests`. `path` is
the route the request was reduced to: no ids and no query string.

id.description: The request's place in the log; a higher id is newer.

responseBytes.description: The response body's length, or `null` when it wasn't known up front.

RelayView.description:
The readable view of the relay connection — everything except the secret
`token`, which stays write-only and is never returned. Mirrors
`RelaySettings` minus `token`. The client prefills these and only re-sends
the relay block (with a fresh token) when the user changes it.

ReplaceTunnelRequestBody.description:
PUT body — a full replace of the visible settings guarded by
`settingsRevision`, plus an optional write-only `relay` block (absent = keep
the stored relay connection, present = replace all four fields).

`publicHost` is required and full-replace: send the desired host as a
string, or `null` to clear it. An omitted field is rejected — full-replace
PUT semantics, and the relay block is the only intentionally-omittable
member (because it's write-only and the client can't echo back what it
hasn't seen).

settingsRevision.description: The optimistic-concurrency token echoed from the last-seen snapshot.

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` that reads the next page, or `null` on the last one.

RequestRefusalBody.description:
Why a bearer gate refused a logged request with a `401`. Mirrors
[`RequestRefusal`].

TunnelStateResponse.description:
Tunnel state on the wire. The relay connection's non-secret fields are
returned in [`RelayView`] (the `token` stays write-only and never appears
here). `settingsRevision` is the optimistic-concurrency token a PUT must echo.

# Liveness is now verified, not optimistic

`status` is the real [`TunnelStatus`] FSM position. `servedOrigin`
resolves to `https://{publicHost}` **only** while `status == "verified"` —
i.e. after a `/health` probe through the public origin came back healthy —
and the supervisor re-probes, so it reverts to the loopback fallback if the
tunnel silently drops. `running` is the coarse "a supervisor is attempting"
view (`dialing`/`verified`/`unreachable`), retained for back-compat; prefer
`status`.
`dialAttempts` counts relay dials for this revision (resets on the next
reconcile) — a counter climbing with a steady `error` flags a permanent
misconfiguration. This is the resolution of
<https://github.com/Assessment-is/Wildflower/issues/184>.

settingsRevision.description:
Which revision of the persisted settings this snapshot reflects — the
optimistic-concurrency token a PUT must echo.

status.description: The liveness FSM position — the authoritative state. See the type docs.

running.description:
`true` when a supervisor is attempting (`dialing`/`verified`/
`unreachable`). A derived view of `status`, kept for back-compat.

dialAttempts.description:
How many times the tunnel has tried to dial the relay for this revision,
resets on the next reconcile. Surfaced so an operator can spot a permanent
misconfiguration (counter climbs with no recovery) without the daemon
having to classify rathole errors itself.

servedOrigin.description:
`https://{publicHost}` only while `status == "verified"`, else the
loopback fallback. See the type-level docs.

oneOf.description:
The relay connection's non-secret fields, or `null` when no relay is
configured. The `token` is never included.

TunnelStatus.description:
The liveness state of the tunnel. The full FSM lives in the tunnel slice;
this is the position consumers care about.

This is also the type the tunnel slice's `/tunnel` HTTP surface serializes
directly (lowercase variants), so it derives `Serialize`/`ToSchema` here
rather than a parallel wire enum re-declaring the same five variants.
